headline_marked: Obaidul Quader and 6 others [[sentenced to death by ICT-2]] for July uprising crimes
headline: Obaidul Quader and 6 others sentenced to death by ICT-2 for July uprising crimes
summary: The International Crimes Tribunal-2 found the senior Awami League leaders guilty of crimes against humanity, including murder and persecution during the mass uprising.
details: The International Crimes Tribunal-2 has sentenced Awami League General Secretary Obaidul Quader and six other senior party and affiliated leaders to death for crimes against humanity during the July-August mass uprising.

The other convicts include former state minister Mohammad Ali Arafat, AL Joint General Secretary Bahauddin Nasim, Jubo League Chairman Sheikh Fazle Shams Parash, General Secretary Moinul Hossain Khan Nikhil, Chhatra League President Saddam Hussain, and General Secretary Sheikh Wali Asif Enan.

The tribunal found the convicts guilty of murder, persecution, and other crimes against humanity committed during the crackdown on protesters. The accused have been absconding throughout the proceedings.
The court also ordered the confiscation of 50 percent of the movable and immovable properties of Quader, Arafat, Nasim, Parash, and Nikhil to compensate victims and the families of those killed.
Justice Nozrul Islam Chowdhury, chairman of the tribunal, read a summary of the 557-page verdict. The full judgment weighed approximately 25kg.
Obaidul Quader was sentenced to death on charges of ordering attacks on quota-reform protesters and failing to prevent mass killings. He was also convicted of directing systematic attacks in August.
Bahauddin Nasim and Mohammad Ali Arafat were also handed death sentences for their roles in the conspiracy to suppress the movement and using state resources to facilitate crimes.
About an hour after the verdict, a crude bomb exploded near the Supreme Court gate. Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed stated that CCTV footage identified suspects who could be 'AL miscreants'.
More than 100 pro-AL lawyers staged a silent protest against the verdict on the Supreme Court premises, chanting 'Joy Bangla, Joy Bangabandhu'.

headline_marked: Saudi Arabia claims [[Houthi drone destroyed near Makkah]]
headline: Saudi Arabia claims Houthi drone destroyed near Makkah
summary: The Saudi-led coalition reports intercepting a drone targeting the holy city, while Houthi rebels deny the attack.
details: Saudi Arabia has accused Iran-aligned Houthi rebels of launching a drone toward the holy city of Makkah. The Saudi-led coalition stated that the drone was detected and shot down by air defense forces on Tuesday evening before it could enter protected airspace.

A spokesperson for the coalition, Turki al-Maliki, condemned the attempt as an effort to spread panic among worshippers and harm civilians. He emphasized that the security of the two holy mosques—Masjid al-Haram and Masjid an-Nabawi—is a priority that will not be compromised.

In response to the threat, the Saudi government briefly issued security alerts in Makkah, Taif, and Jeddah. These alerts were lifted within minutes, marking the first time since 2017 that such warnings had been issued for Makkah.

Houthi rebels have strongly denied the allegations, calling them 'misinformation.' A military source from the Houthis stated that they never target holy sites and categorically denied any threat from Yemen toward Makkah.

The tension comes amid a broader conflict that began in 2015, when Houthi rebels seized the capital, Sana'a, and ousted the internationally recognized government. Saudi Arabia intervened to support the government, leading to a prolonged war.
Recent escalations include Houthi attacks on civilian infrastructure in Khamis Mushait, Abha, and Taif, which reportedly injured 13 civilians and damaged several homes and vehicles.

The conflict is further complicated by the Houthi's strategic control over the Red Sea coast and the Bab al-Mandab Strait, threatening to close the vital shipping lane to increase pressure on the Saudi-led coalition.
